Dynamic Nelson-Siegel Model Dynamics

Source: R/dns-dynamics.r
estimate_dns_dynamics.Rd

Functions to estimate and analyze the dynamics of DNS model factors.

Estimates the stochastic dynamics of the factors in the Dynamic Nelson-Siegel model based on historical factor time series.

Usage

estimate_dns_dynamics(
  params_df,
  min_observations = 20,
  dt = NULL,
  sampling = c("monthly", "daily"),
  structure = c("diagonal", "full")
)

Arguments

params_df

Data frame. The parameters data frame from fit_dns_model() containing columns for Date, beta1, beta2, beta3. With sampling = "daily" the corresponding change columns are also required; with sampling = "monthly" they are recomputed internally on the month-end grid and need not be present.

min_observations

Integer. Minimum number of observations required for estimation, counted on the series the regression actually runs on (month-ends when sampling = "monthly").

dt

Numeric. Time step in years of the series the regression runs on. Defaults to the sampling mode's spacing: 1/12 for "monthly", 1/252 for "daily". With sampling = "monthly" the step is month-end to month-end by construction, so a conflicting value is ignored with a warning.

sampling

Character. "monthly" (default) subsamples the factor series to its last observation per month before estimating; "daily" estimates on the series as given, preserving the pre-0.2.0 behavior.

structure

Character. "diagonal" (the default) estimates three independent Ornstein-Uhlenbeck processes with correlated innovations, as earlier versions did. "full" regresses each factor change on the levels of all three factors, giving the full mean-reversion matrix of the Diebold-Li VAR(1), in which a shock to one factor can pull the others.

Value

A list containing:

  • For each factor (beta1, beta2, beta3):

    • kappa: Mean reversion speed

    • theta: Long-run mean

    • sigma: Volatility

    • model: Fitted regression model

    • half_life: Half-life of mean reversion (in days)

    • summary: Basic statistics about the factor

    • se: Standard errors of kappa, theta and sigma

    • t_value: t statistics for kappa and theta against zero

    • half_life_ci: 95 percent confidence interval for the half-life, in years

  • correlation: Correlation matrix of factor innovations

  • innovations: Matrix of factor innovations (residuals from mean reversion)

  • innovation_dates: Date vector aligned with the rows of innovations

  • estimation_period: Date range used for estimation

  • sampling, dt: The sampling mode and time step actually used

  • structure: The mean-reversion structure estimated

  • kappa_matrix: The 3 by 3 mean-reversion matrix. Diagonal under structure = "diagonal"; the estimated VAR(1) matrix under "full"

  • theta_vector: Long-run means as a vector, named by factor

  • eigenvalues, system_stability: Eigenvalues of kappa_matrix and whether every real part is positive

Details

This function implements the estimation of an Ornstein-Uhlenbeck process for each factor: $$d\beta(t) = \kappa(\theta - \beta(t))dt + \sigma dW(t)$$ The discretized version used for estimation is: $$\Delta\beta(t) = \kappa(\theta - \beta(t-1))\Delta t + \sigma\epsilon(t)$$

The default month-end sampling follows Diebold-Li practice. Daily cross-sectional refits carry measurement noise that is serially uncorrelated; estimating the OU regression on daily changes reads that noise as mean reversion and inflates kappa by an order of magnitude (errors-in-variables), which in turn makes fixed-step simulation of the resulting dynamics numerically unstable. Month-end sampling averages the noise down and recovers reversion speeds on the economically meaningful time scale. Subsampling is idempotent: passing an already month-end series through sampling = "monthly" reproduces it unchanged.

Standard errors come from the fitted regression. For kappa the mapping from the slope is linear, so \(se(\kappa) = se(b) / \Delta t\). For theta, which is a ratio of coefficients, they come from the delta method. The one for sigma is the asymptotic \(\sigma / \sqrt{2(n-k)}\). Note that kappa carries a well-known upward small-sample bias of order \(5 / T\) in a sample of \(T\) years, which these standard errors do not capture: they describe the sampling noise, not the bias.

With structure = "full" the system estimated is $$\Delta\beta(t) = K(\theta - \beta(t-1))\Delta t + \Sigma\epsilon(t),$$ so each change is regressed on all three lagged levels. Writing the fitted intercepts as \(a\) and slopes as \(B\), the mean-reversion matrix is \(K = -B / \Delta t\) and the long-run mean is \(\theta = K^{-1} a / \Delta t\). The per-factor kappa entries then hold the diagonal of \(K\); the cross terms are only in kappa_matrix, and simulate_dns_factors uses the diagonal.

Examples

data(treasury_yields)

# The default monthly sampling estimates on month-end observations, so
# fitting only those is enough and is an order of magnitude quicker.
# warm_start = FALSE makes each cross-section independent of which other
# dates are in the panel, so these fits are identical to the ones fitting
# every day would produce on the same month-ends.
month_ends <- treasury_yields[
  !duplicated(format(treasury_yields$Date, "%Y-%m"), fromLast = TRUE),
]
dns_result <- fit_dns_model(month_ends, n_days = nrow(month_ends),
                            show_progress = FALSE, warm_start = FALSE)
#> Warning: Parameters rest on a bound in some fits: lambda on 13 (of 72 dates). The factor decomposition is not identified on those dates; see the at_bound element of the result, pass wider lower_bounds/upper_bounds, or check the yield scale.

dynamics <- estimate_dns_dynamics(dns_result$parameters)
dynamics
#> DNS factor dynamics
#>   estimated on     2019-02-28 to 2024-12-31
#>   sampling         monthly (dt = 1/12), 71 observations
#>   structure        diagonal
#> 
#>                 kappa se_kappa   theta  sigma half_life_y
#> level (b1)     2.7753   0.9339  0.0346 0.0304      0.2498
#> slope (b2)     2.6320   0.8909 -0.0083 0.0330      0.2634
#> curvature (b3) 2.1218   0.8195 -0.0043 0.0579      0.3267
#> 
#>   stable           TRUE (eigenvalues 2.775 2.632 2.122)

# Standard errors show how weakly kappa is identified in a short sample
dynamics$beta1$se
#>       kappa       theta       sigma 
#> 0.933902253 0.004531378 0.002584906 
dynamics$beta1$half_life_ci
#>     lower     upper 
#> 0.1504970 0.7335731 

# The full VAR(1), in which a shock to one factor pulls the others
full <- estimate_dns_dynamics(dns_result$parameters, structure = "full")
round(full$kappa_matrix, 3)
#>        beta1  beta2  beta3
#> beta1  3.746 -3.289 -0.031
#> beta2 -5.999  3.251 -1.160
#> beta3  4.821  4.394  4.768
